summary.text: Brittany Pettersen is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 7th District, first elected in 2022 as the first woman to represent the district. A Jefferson County native, she served a decade in the Colorado legislature before Congress and sits on the House Financial Services Committee. Her official biography says she is focused on mental health and substance use treatment, housing affordability, and consumer protection.

paragraphs.text: Born in Colorado and raised in Jefferson County. According to her campaign website, her father was a construction contractor and her mother a hairdresser, and her mother's addiction after being prescribed opioids shaped her interest in behavioral health policy.

Describes herself as the first in her family to graduate from both high school and college. Earned a B.A. in political science from Metropolitan State University of Denver, which her official biography says she paid for by waiting tables.
Before running for office, worked for New Era Colorado, a nonprofit that works to increase youth participation in politics.

Served in the Colorado House of Representatives (District 28) from 2013 to 2019. According to her campaign website, she chaired the House Education Committee and passed the Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, a red flag law, and the Secure Savings Act.

Served in the Colorado State Senate (District 22) from 2019 to 2023. Her official biography says her state legislative work included legislation on health care costs, the opioid epidemic, reproductive health care, and child care.

Won the open 7th District seat in 2022, defeating Republican Erik Aadland with about 56% of the vote, and was re-elected in 2024 over Republican Sergei Matveyuk with about 55%. She was unopposed in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee, including the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance and as Vice Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions, according to her official biography.
According to her official biography, she lives in Lakewood with her husband, Ian, and their two sons.
